description: ERA5-HEAT is the Copernicus Climate Data Store product of mean radiant temperature and Universal Thermal Climate Index derived from ERA5. The current version 1.1 covers 1940 to near real time on a 0.25-degree grid from 90 degrees north to 60 degrees south. Hourly fields and aggregated statistics support heat-exposure analysis, including indicators such as tropical nights. ECMWF supplies NetCDF files under the Licence to use Copernicus Products, with free acquisition through a registered CDS account. The fields can drive outdoor heat-exposure simulations, compare cooling interventions and identify thermal stress around critical facilities. They complement data-era5-reanalysis by converting meteorological variables into human thermal-comfort indices. The grid does not resolve street geometry, shade or individual physiology, and coverage excludes Antarctica. Local urban models still require finer geometry and boundary conditions. The current start year extends the period described in the original paper; the provider identifies version 1.0 as deprecated. No account sign-in was needed to inspect the public metadata.
